origins.section: Escalation Turns a Price Quoted in One Year Into the Price Paid in Another
Real Dollars Pair With a Real Rate, Nominal Dollars With a Nominal Rate
Only Escalation Above Inflation Changes a Real Model

gates.says: all 3 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-base-year: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-base-year: 'The exponent counts the years from the price base year to the year of payment': 500 x 1.04^(2028-2025) = 562.4.
recorded.prompt:q-mix: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-mix: 'Nominal flows at a real rate count inflation in the flows and never take it out: the cost looks $143k bigger.'
recorded.prompt:q-steel: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-steel: e_real = (1+e)/(1+i) - 1, and 1.05/1.03 - 1 is about 1.94%; 'What a real model needs is the real escalation, the part above inflation.'

recorded.prompt:q-base-year:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-base-year:a: 'This course measures escalation from the price base year, never from the project's start.'
recorded.prompt:q-base-year:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-base-year:b: The exponent is y - b = 2028 - 2025 = 3, not 2.
recorded.prompt:q-base-year:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-base-year:d: c(1+e)^(y-b) gives exponent 3; a payment in the base year itself 'is not escalated at all'.
recorded.prompt:q-mix:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-mix:b: That describes the other mix, real flows at a nominal rate; nominal flows at a real rate are 'too large'.
recorded.prompt:q-mix:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-mix:c: Inflation cancels only for consistent pairs; 'the two mixes err in opposite directions'.
recorded.prompt:q-mix:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-mix:d: Reference table: 'nominal flows, real rate | too large'.
recorded.prompt:q-steel:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-steel:a: 'not 4.5% (that would count inflation twice)' - the full nominal rise is wrong in a real model.
recorded.prompt:q-steel:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-steel:b: 'and not 0% (that would ignore the part of the rise that is real)'.
recorded.prompt:q-steel:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-steel:c: Real escalation is (1+e)/(1+i) - 1, which removes inflation; adding inflation on top contradicts it.
